item.text:
**3B.6 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024**

**Working judgment:** `Partial / limited yes`. Marcos and his administration did take some steps that can reduce fear, especially around disinformation response and information access. But the broader 2024 record still shows red-tagging, threats to journalists and activists, and a coercive information environment. I did not find evidence that Marcos replaced insurgent or criminal violence with open state terror, but I also did not find evidence that he fully broke the fear climate.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Positive | Gov’t vows legal action vs deep fake video creators, spreaders | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-26 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-vows-legal-action-vs-deep-fake-video-creators-spreaders/ | The government said DICT and the NSC were investigating a manipulated deepfake video of Marcos and considering legal action. This is a reactive but real effort to contain panic and misinformation rather than amplify it. | 3B.6, 3B.5 |
| Positive | PCO to designate ‘fact-check officers’ in state media to fight fake news | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-09-09 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pco-to-designate-fact-check-officers-in-state-media-to-fight-fake-news/ | PCO said it would place fact-check officers in state media and stated there was no policy or practice of red-tagging in the Marcos administration. This is the clearest formal anti-disinformation step I found in 2024. | 3B.6, 3B.3, 3B.4 |
| Positive | The government expanded public access through the eFOI portal and kept a media-literacy / disinformation campaign in place | Philippine News Agency | 2024-01-18 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217036 | Expanded eFOI access and a standing media-literacy/disinformation campaign support a lower-fear environment in digital governance. This is modest evidence of a non-coercive response model. | 3B.6, 3B.4 |
| Positive | DOJ creates task force to review EJK cases | Philippine News Agency | 2024-11-06 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1237266 | The DOJ created a task force to investigate drug-war EJKs and file charges if warranted. That can reduce fear indirectly by signaling that abuse can be examined rather than normalized. | 3B.6, 3B.4, 3B.1 |
| Negative | Philippines: “I turned my fear into courage”: Red-tagging and state violence against young human rights defenders in the Philippines | Amnesty International | 2024-10-14 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa35/8574/2024/en/ | Amnesty says Marcos-era actors weaponized digital tools, misinformation, and the anti-terror law to create fear, and that red-tagging vilified activists, journalists, teachers, and others as “communists” or “terrorists.” This is direct evidence of a continuing fear climate. | 3B.6, 3B.3, 3B.5 |
| Negative | World Report 2024: Philippines | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/philippines | HRW says red-tagging by authorities and government supporters continued and often preceded physical attack, constraining democratic space. This undercuts any claim that fear was broadly reduced. | 3B.6, 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Negative | Philippines | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines | The report says red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats against journalists persisted under Marcos, despite a somewhat more media-friendly stance than Duterte’s. That points to a still-coercive atmosphere rather than a cleaned-up public sphere. | 3B.6, 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Negative | Philippines: Dangerous “Red Tagging” of Labor Leaders | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-25 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders | HRW reports officials and police or military members threatened union leaders by linking them to communism. This is strong evidence of tolerated intimidation rather than a reduced-fear environment. | 3B.6, 3B.3, 3B.2 |

**Synthesis**
- Marcos did make some anti-fear moves in 2024: deepfake response, fact-checking in state media, broader information access, and an EJK review task force.
- Those steps were real, but they were limited and mostly reactive.
- Independent reporting still describes a coercive climate built around red-tagging, threats, and disinformation.
- So the best reading is: `some reduction in informational insecurity, but not enough to say Marcos avoided replacing violence with a broader political fear climate`.

**Search gap**
- I did not find evidence that Marcos personally used classic emergency powers or mass repression to create fear in 2024.
- The main problem was not a single overt state-terror program; it was persistent red-tagging, intimidation, and enforcement pressure tolerated within the system.
